correctness.rationale: In the exact coefficient norm the basis action sends e_1 to e_0 and e_n to w_n e_{m(n-1)} for n>=2, with distinct targets. Thus the two Gram operators are diagonal and the commutator diagonal is -1 at zero, and w_k^2 minus the unique incoming square w_{k/m+1}^2 when m divides k. Exponential decay beats every polynomial for fixed h, also for every positive Schatten exponent. The finite trace sum telescopes with incoming indices 1 through floor(N/m)+1; the limit is zero. Nonmultiples are positive; on multiples the outgoing/incoming weight-square ratio tends to zero for fixed h. For h tending to zero, h^2 times the outgoing and incoming squares converge away from x=0 to A(x) and C(x)=A(x/m), respectively, uniformly on compact scaled intervals. The exact factors (1-1/n)^s are uniformly bounded for n>=2, so scaled weights near zero are O(x^2+h^2), with exponential tails bounded by a polynomial times exp(-x/m). This proves the local law on the m separate residue classes, and exponential domination extends it to |y|^p for every fixed p>0 and to a supremum limit. The only positive zero of A-C solves exp(2x(1-1/m))=m^2; max(A)=max(C)=m^s exp(-2), attained asymptotically by the outgoing-only branch. The limiting signed integral is zero since integral C=m integral A. Twice the negative mass gives the stated trace coefficient by integrating x^2 exp(-a*x) above the zero. For p=2 the combined integral is 2 integral A^2 minus (2/m) integral AC; the x^4 gamma integrals give exactly the stated coefficient. Small exceptional indices do not affect any limit.
